clue.text: Food heard to be doled out at intervals

indicators.note: something heard is taken by ear, so we want a word spelt differently that sounds the same as the food

explanation.surface: Some food that sounds as though it is rationed out bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: CEREAL and SERIAL sound identical; the spelling comes from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial is a story published in instalments, issued at regular intervals rather than all at once.

clue.text: Got wind of an unconventional descent

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual form, so the letters are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone heard rumours of an unorthodox climb down.
explanation.definitionFit: To scent something is to smell it, and getting wind of is the idiom for smelling or sensing.

clue.text: Originally, rugby union pro evaded extradition for forging currency

indicators.note: originally points to the start of each word, so we keep only the first letters

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A rugby player who escaped extradition for counterfeiting money.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the unit of money used in India, Pakistan and elsewhere.

clue.text: Anna held a number of receptive devices

definitions.note: plural definition: ANTENNA is also an accepted plural (more often antennas) for aerials

indicators.note: held means kept in someone's grasp, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written; it is split around the number

explanation.surface: Anna was holding several radio aerials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number of' looks like 'several'; here 'a number' is a specific one, TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Antennae or antennas are aerials, devices that receive radio signals; in the clue it is a plural noun.

clue.text: Appalled at gash, newly made

indicators.note: something newly made is formed afresh, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone horrified at a fresh wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means struck with horror or shock, a close synonym of appalled.

clue.text: Plot is in terrible danger!

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters are thrown into a different order

explanation.surface: A conspiracy is under serious threat!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' reads as a scheme in danger; it is a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a cultivated plot of ground beside a house.

clue.text: Fool the Queen into, perhaps, making a statement

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word is only one possible arrangement, so its letters can be reordered

explanation.surface: Someone tricking the Queen into making a declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' looks like a verb with the Queen as its object; it is a noun. ER is the Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a confident declaration of something as fact, a kind of statement.

clue.text: Thanks to single daughter with long claws …

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Gratitude to an only daughter whose fingernails are long; the ellipsis carries on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Talons are the long hooked claws of a bird of prey, so taloned means having such claws.

clue.text: that can be compared this way?

definitions.text: that can be compared this way?

parts.words: that can be compared this way?
parts.note: surface reading: following on from the daughter with long claws, how might her claws be compared?
setter's reading: a simile for someone tough, using the word for fingernails

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the woman with long claws could be described like this.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue's long claws; claws are nails, and the stock simile for a tough, unfeeling person uses them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person who is tough and unsympathetic, and the long-clawed daughter fits it both literally and figuratively.

clue.text: Look for exercise on old disc

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
an EP (extended play) is an old record format

explanation.surface: Checking an old record for a workout routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is a quick look, so the noun works as a synonym for a glance.

clue.text: Examine the outcome of a sporting challenge

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at how a sporting contest finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'outcome' does double duty: it is part of the wordplay and also of the definition. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is a top-level cricket contest, so its final score is literally a Test result.

clue.text: Widespread western movement omits English contribution

indicators.note: movement shifts things about, so the remaining letters change places
omits tells us to leave a letter out of the word

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English; one E is dropped

explanation.surface: A broad movement in the West that leaves out the English.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one E from WESTERN, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Things strewn are scattered over an area, so the word describes something spread widely.

clue.text: Seaman in search of adventure is not normal

parts.note: as in a knight errant, roaming in search of adventure

explanation.surface: A sailor seeking thrills is behaving oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant means departing from the usual or expected course, the opposite of normal.

clue.text: Lazy workforce old Nick may employ?

definitions.text: Lazy workforce old Nick may employ?

parts.note: surface reading: a team of workers who will not pull their weight
setter's reading: the proverb says the Devil finds work for this

explanation.surface: A slack staff that the Devil would happily hire.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is the Devil; the proverb runs 'the Devil makes work for idle hands'. Hands are also workers, and idle means lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names inactive people as the ones Satan recruits, and hands is a standard word for labourers.

clue.text: Spectacle seen from space harries ET somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified manner, so the letters can be arranged in any way that works

explanation.surface: An alien (ET, from the film) is pestered by some sight in outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthrise is the view of our planet coming up over the Moon's horizon, famously photographed by Apollo 8.

clue.text: Generous type

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a sort or variety

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a generous sort of person; split, it is an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning benevolent and also a noun meaning a sort or class.

clue.text: A patch of ground in an Israeli city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a unit of land area
second meaning: the port also called Akko, in northern Israel

explanation.surface: A plot of land somewhere in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an old measure of land area and the name of an ancient port city in Israel.

clue.text: Unusual lama can be seen in yearbook

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters fall in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: An odd Tibetan monk appears in an annual publication.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a book published each year with a calendar and data, so it is a yearbook.

clue.text: Masonry to rebuild study that looks heavenward

indicators.note: to rebuild is to put the bricks together again in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Stonework being rebuilt for an observatory, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy is the scientific study of the stars and planets, the sky above us.

clue.text: Live outside university with the rest

indicators.note: outside means wrapped around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Living off campus along with everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is whatever remains after the main part is gone, the leftover remainder.

clue.text: The fellow has an appointment, an official commission

explanation.surface: A man with a scheduled meeting about his formal assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an authorisation or instruction given officially, a commission to act.

clue.text: Sailor idle, even when all fired up

parts.note: to laze is to be idle

explanation.surface: A sailor stays lazy even when everyone else is excited.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze means burning fiercely, and figuratively fired up or full of passion.

clue.text: Class of creatures one male Greek character bans in Athens, initially

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of each of the words is kept

parts.note: first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A Greek character in Athens who bans a class of creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphibia is the zoological class containing frogs, toads, newts and other amphibians.

clue.text: Season well

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the time of year after winter
second meaning: a natural source of water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Season well' looks like a cooking instruction; it is two separate nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the season between winter and summer and also a place where water rises from the ground.

clue.text: Drinker turned up to put plant in new container

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word reads from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drinker showed up to tend a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot is to move a plant from one pot into another, usually a larger one.

clue.text: Peerless international organisation in front when opponent intervened

indicators.note: something that intervened has come between, so it sits inside another word

parts.note: to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A world body that stays ahead even when challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrivalled means having no equal, just as peerless means having no peer.

clue.text: Amusement caused by madcap laying trap

indicators.note: a trap holds something inside it, so the letters sit caught within the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: Fun from a wild prankster setting a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Play is activity done for enjoyment, a synonym of amusement or recreation.

clue.text: About machine part that's ingenious

parts.note: a lever is a component of a machine

explanation.surface: Something to do with a smart bit of machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and ingenious both describe quick inventive intelligence, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: "The French bête" initially translated as "insect"

indicators.note: translated means carried into another form, so the letters are converted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the accent

explanation.surface: A French phrase for an animal, rendered into English as insect.
explanation.walkthrough: Bête is French for beast, so it looks as if a real translation is wanted; instead the letters of LE BETE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect with hard wing cases, so insect is its general class.
